newsitem.title: PERU: Peru frees 45 people wrongly jailed for terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Peru frees 45 people wrongly jailed for terrorism.

text.p: Peru on Wednesday released another 45 prisoners who were jailed unjustly as terrorists during the state's ongoing war against communist guerrillas.
A decree published in the government daily El Peruano and signed by President Alberto Fujimori announced pardons for the prisoners serving sentences in 15 jails around the country.

Their release brings to 76 the number of innocent inmates freed on the recommendation of a new government-appointed commission examining the cases for pardons among the more than 3,000 prisoners in Peruvian jails on terrorism charges.

The government, which has since 1995 released about 300 prisoners wrongly accused of terrorism, admits more than 300 others could still be unfairly behind bars. Human rights groups say the number could be as high as 1,000.

Most of these prisoners were put behind bars by Peru's controversial "faceless" courts, whose anonymous judges often wear hoods or sit behind one-way screens. Despite the errors committed by the secret court system and the torrent of criticism from rights groups at home and abroad, Congress voted last week to extend the courts for another year.

Government spokesmen said the courts were still necessary in the war on the Maoist Shining Path guerrillas and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) movement. Conflicts sparked by these two groups have cost 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.

Although greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, Shining Path has been flexing its muscles this year with a series of car bombs, assassinations and clashes with security forces.
